s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic progressive respiratory and systemic syndrome with exertional dyspnea, orthopnea, and lower limb swelling, complicated by interstitial lung disease and autoimmune condition
salient_findings: Bilateral lower limb swelling worse in evenings
Bilateral ulnar deviation at metacarpophalangeal joints with swan neck deformities
key_facts: 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement
Interstitial lung disease four years prior
Vital signs: BP 138/86 mmHg, pulse 85/min, temperature 96.5°F (35.8°C), BMI 16.3 kg/m², respiratory rate 20/min, oxygen saturation 93% on 3L oxygen
No skin rashes, ulcerations, palpable purpura, or nodules
Bilateral ulnar deviation at metacarpophalangeal joints with swan neck deformities

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Autoimmune condition with joint involvement, interstitial lung disease, and low complement levels

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement, high rheumatoid factor, and swan neck deformities

shortlist.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca and autoimmune condition with joint involvement

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of autoimmune conditions, including interstitial lung disease and joint involvement

shortlist.label: Systemic Sclerosis

raw.rationale: The patient has a 20-year history of autoimmune condition with joint involvement, bilateral ulnar deviation at metacarpophalangeal joints with swan neck deformities, and high rheumatoid factor levels (>1000 kIU/L), which are characteristic of Rheumatoid Arthritis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: While the patient has some features that could be seen in SLE, such as interstitial lung disease and low complement levels, the primary presentation and long history of joint involvement point more strongly towards Rheumatoid Arthritis.

rejected.label: Sjögren's Syndrome
rejected.why: Keratoconjunctivitis sicca is a feature of Sjögren's Syndrome, but the patient's primary symptoms and history are more consistent with Rheumatoid Arthritis.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's presentation does not clearly meet the criteria for Mixed Connective Tissue Disease, which typically involves a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.

rejected.label: Systemic Sclerosis
rejected.why: There is no mention of skin thickening or other characteristic features of Systemic Sclerosis, making this diagnosis less likely.
